![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c72489a2d33a181fe7bc07d5cc017b93daccac51889cbb61edd64d4ee34429df.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}},\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/98aa4c0a436e4649ccd3d48a53fbf94b0341bf30b95745c4d052381680d223cf.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/47380c108c5b271761de2a027399bbd5981f2a9bdff21e498d73d0b430d070c7.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$
